data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate reported a gross prior year reserve release of GBP 67.7 million in 2021, representing a 2.03% reduction of opening gross claims outstanding. This overall release was driven by favorable claims development in the Insurance and Reinsurance divisions, including releases related to the absence of 2020 COVID losses and prior year catastrophe events. However, the Discontinued lines experienced significant adverse development totaling GBP 94.0 million, primarily due to strengthening in US trucking liability, International Casualty, Contractors sub-class of US Casualty, Aviation, and other UK P&C classes, partially offset by a release in Pro Rata. The syndicate also noted the impact of the Supreme Court ruling on business interruption claims and the heightened inflationary environment as factors influencing reserving.

The Supreme Court ruling issued on 15 January 2021, reflecting the benchmark case on policy wordings, brought a degree of certainty to many, but not all, matters relating to coverage of this extremely unusual event and enabled the settlement of many of those claims
the impact of the heightened inflationary environment that has emerged following the pandemic

Reserve releases of GBP 23.0 million in 2021 compare favourably to 2020 which saw a strengthening of GBP 12.0 million. Reserve releases were driven by favourable performance in a host of classes, including Cargo, Marine Liability, Commercial Property (driven by prior year cat releases), War, Financial Lines, and Credit.

COVID losses in 2020 totalled GBP 39.0 million compared to a GBP 7.0 million release in 2021. Additionally, the Reinsurance division benefitted from GBP 24.0 million of net reserve releases in 2021 (driven by favourable performance in Cat NA and Cat International) compared to a strengthening of GBP 17.0 million in 2020.

reserve strengthening. Adverse reserve development totalled GBP 94.0 million in 2021 compared to releases of GBP 14.0 million in 2020. The strengthening is predominantly driven by US trucking liability (GBP 33.0 million) and International Casualty (GBP 38.0 million) classes, which saw significant deterioration in the year, driven by adverse experience, changes to the development pattern and prior loss ratios. Further deteriorations include the Contractors sub-class of the US Casualty book, Aviation, plus other P&C UK classes. These are partially offset by a release in Pro Rata.

data.data_quality_notes: The gross prior year development figure of -67.7m from the 'Net outstanding claims' reconciliation table on page 11 contradicts the +161.4m strengthening calculated from the gross claims development triangle on page 12. The figure from the reconciliation table is prioritized as it is an explicit line item for prior year movements. The discrepancy may be due to the impact of the Part VII transfer (RITC) in 2020 and subsequent reporting changes, which could affect the interpretation of the claims development triangle. Additionally, the sum of specific LOB movements mentioned in the narrative (net releases of GBP 23.0m in Insurance, net releases of GBP 24.0m in Reinsurance, and gross adverse development of GBP 94.0m in Discontinued lines) does not reconcile to the overall gross prior year development of -67.7m, likely due to the LOB figures being net of reinsurance or not fully comprehensive.
